questions.question: What is Spokane's official nickname?
questions.explanation: Spokane has been called "The Lilac City" since the early 1900s â€” lilacs thrive in the Inland Northwest climate. The annual Lilac Festival (since 1938) is one of the longest-running spring festivals in the U.S.

questions.question: What is the largest single employer in Spokane County?
questions.explanation: Providence Health Services is the largest employer in Spokane County, with over 8,000 employees across its hospitals and clinics â€” including Sacred Heart Medical Center & Children's Hospital. Fairchild Air Force Base employs roughly 2,900 (about 2,200 active-duty Air Force personnel plus 700 civilians).

questions.question: What major international event did Spokane host in 1974?
questions.explanation: Expo '74 ran from May to November 1974 with the theme "Celebrating Tomorrow's Fresh, New Environment." It transformed an old rail yard into what is now Riverfront Park, and remains the smallest U.S. city to ever host a World's Fair.

questions.question: Spokane Falls is one of the largest urban waterfalls in North America. What is the total drop in elevation across the falls?
questions.explanation: The total drop across the Upper and Lower Spokane Falls is approximately 146 feet, making it one of the highest-volume urban waterfalls in the U.S. â€” even bigger than Niagara during peak spring runoff.

questions.question: The word "Spokane" comes from the Salish language. What is the most commonly cited translation?
questions.explanation: "Children of the Sun" is the most widely accepted translation. The Spokane Tribe (spÌ“qÌ“nÌ“iÊ”) has lived along the Spokane River for thousands of years before European contact.

questions.question: Riverfront Park's iconic 155-foot clock tower is the only remaining piece of which historic structure?
questions.explanation: The clock tower was built in 1902 as part of the Great Northern Railway Depot. The depot itself was demolished to make way for Expo '74, but the tower was preserved as a centerpiece of the new Riverfront Park.

questions.question: Which industry sector employs the most people in the Spokane region?
questions.explanation: Health Care & Social Assistance is the #1 employment sector in Spokane, accounting for roughly 1 in 5 jobs in the region. Spokane serves as the medical hub for the Inland Northwest, drawing patients from eastern Washington, North Idaho, western Montana, and parts of Oregon.

questions.question: The Spokane Tribe Reservation, established in 1881, is located primarily in which Washington county?
questions.explanation: The Spokane Indian Reservation is located in Stevens County, with tribal headquarters in Wellpinit. It covers about 159,000 acres on the west side of the Spokane River. The Tribe never signed a treaty with the U.S. government â€” the reservation was established by executive order.

questions.question: Which native salmon species was a vital food source for the Spokane Tribe but was effectively eliminated from the upper Spokane River after construction of Grand Coulee Dam (completed 1942)?
questions.explanation: Grand Coulee Dam blocked Chinook salmon migration past the dam, eliminating salmon runs that had sustained the Spokane Tribe for thousands of years. The Tribe never received compensation for the loss until a 2019 settlement. Reintroduction efforts are ongoing.

questions.question: What is the highest natural point in Spokane County?
questions.explanation: Mt. Spokane tops out at 5,887 feet — the highest point in Spokane County. Abercrombie (Pend Oreille County) and Quartz Mountain (Stevens County) are both taller, but they're outside Spokane County. Mt. Spokane State Park is the largest state park in Washington at over 13,900 acres.
